familyFit.summary: BabyDrive’s 2022 AWD test fitted named three-restraint combinations; your exact three-forward-facing/booster arrangement is still pending.
familyFit.row2: Two outer ISOFIX and three rear-backrest top tethers.
familyFit.row3: No third row on this five-seat configuration.
familyFit.testedSeats: BabyDrive 2022 AWD: two InfaSecure Attain More seats plus an InfaSecure Achieve More in the centre. Forward/rear-facing combinations are reported; the article does not document every three-seat orientation or a three-booster trial.
familyFit.buckleAccess: Try the exact boosters and buckles. ANCAP’s selected Type E (4–8 years) booster failed centre installation while the selected Type F (4–10 years) passed; this is specific to those tested restraints.

familyFit.ventilation: Rear pillar air vents in the independently tested AWD.

ownershipUpdates.serviceInterval: MY22-and-earlier: confirm original passport’s 12 months / 15,000 km schedule. MY23 Dynamiq/Techniq maker release and current Genuine Service Plan terms distinguish MY23-and-later EVs at 24 months / 30,000 km. Whichever comes first; severe-use and coolant work can differ. Australian MY23 owner manual p9-8 separately lists low-conductivity coolant replacement at 36 months / 60,000 km and 12V battery inspection at 12 months / 15,000 km, whichever comes first; these do not inherit the two-year general-service interval.
ownershipUpdates.serviceBasis: ESTIMATE: A$400/year midpoint (A$250–550), across differing early/later schedules. A current Australian road test reports A$667/689 two-year dealer visits (about A$339/year over eight years); independent 48-month booking examples are lower and may cover a different scope. Allow age/coolant uncertainty. Obtain the VIN schedule; dealer servicing is required for the newer 7-year extension. Excludes tyres and fault repairs. Hyundai prepaid terms limit new-car plans to the first five services for MY22-and-earlier EVs or first two for MY23-and-later EVs; a remaining plan transfers with the car. A plan is not a guaranteed lifelong tariff. MY23 coolant can fall between ordinary service visits: have the dealer identify prepaid/capped-price inclusions and off-cycle work. No fresh Australian model-specific coolant tariff was verified, so historical visit prices are not represented as a guaranteed all-inclusive maintenance total.
warrantyCautions: Older cars originally have 5-year unlimited-kilometre private-use cover. The 7-year offer is for eligible first registrations from 1 June 2025 and requires on-time authorised-dealer servicing for the extension.
Remaining vehicle cover transfers, but prior commercial use and service history can change eligibility. Confirm the original passport.

HV battery cover is 8 years / 160,000 km. Current terms specify a 70% state-of-health threshold and usage / maintenance conditions; confirm applicable original terms. The 12V battery has 2 years / 40,000 km.

Australian manufacturer statements reported by Drive in May 2026 describe 15-year/300,000-km ICCU cover from first registration for Ioniq 5 built 2 April 2021–14 February 2024. This is reported component cover, not a verified VIN-specific contract; obtain written eligibility and exclusions from the Australian dealer.

risks.title: Superseding ICCU software recall
risks.detail: REC-006224 covers selected 2021–2024 Ioniq 5 / 6 VINs and replaces REC-005942. Confirm the later campaign is complete; the notice specifies a software update.
risks.priceBasis: Applicable official recall update is free. The separate paid ICCU scenario below applies only if recall, warranty, extended cover and other remedies do not cover the fault.
risks.warranty: Australian manufacturer statements reported by Drive in May 2026 describe 15-year/300,000-km ICCU cover from first registration for Ioniq 5 built 2 April 2021–14 February 2024. This is reported component cover, not a verified VIN-specific contract; obtain written eligibility and exclusions from the Australian dealer. Recall rectification remains free for affected VINs; use a paid stress case only when every applicable remedy is unavailable.

risks.title: Full traction-battery replacement — stress case
risks.detail: Budget for a complete pack only if diagnosis supports replacement. A module, control-system or drive-unit-only repair can be substantially cheaper; this range does not predict failure.
risks.priceBasis: ESTIMATE: model-specific Australian quote unavailable; based on the Insurance Council’s 2024 A$7,500–30,000 benchmark (itself converted from US research, not Australian installed invoices) and a broker’s A$10,000–30,000+ general guide, adjusted for the family’s 72.6–84 kWh packs; upper end includes a larger-pack allowance. Full replacement planning total assumes parts, labour and GST; not a hard ceiling or a priced repair offer.
risks.warranty: Current policy conditions and 70% threshold apply only as specified in the relevant warranty.

risks.title: Windscreen replacement and calibration example
risks.detail: A glass-only cash repair is separate from manufacturing warranty. The owner’s insurance excess may be lower; this estimate is the repair bill, not an insurance excess or full collision budget.
risks.priceBasis: ESTIMATE: Ioniq-5-specific quote unavailable; Gold Coast specialist guidance is A$850–1,500 for ADAS/HUD glass. Widened for genuine/acoustic glass and calibration scope. Assumes installed glass, calibration and GST; confirm supplier inclusions and insurance treatment.
risks.warranty: Accident-related costs depend on insurance cover; ordinary manufacturing warranty is not accident insurance.

risks.title: ICCU hardware replacement if all cover is unavailable
risks.detail: Conditional paid stress case only: first confirm recall, original warranty, any ICCU extension and other remedies. This is not added as a routine annual cost and implies no failure probability.
risks.priceBasis: ESTIMATE: Australian model-specific quote unavailable; first-party US OEM ICCU listing is about US$1,297–1,855 for Ioniq 5. Illustrative US$1=A$1.50, plus 10% GST/import/parts variation and roughly A$800–2,000 diagnosis, labour, coolant/fuse allowance. Foreign part is a pricing proxy, not confirmed Australian-VIN fitment; not a live FX or installation quote.
risks.warranty: Australian manufacturer statements reported by Drive in May 2026 describe 15-year/300,000-km ICCU cover from first registration for Ioniq 5 built 2 April 2021–14 February 2024. This is reported component cover, not a verified VIN-specific contract; obtain written eligibility and exclusions from the Australian dealer. Recall rectification remains free for affected VINs; use a paid stress case only when every applicable remedy is unavailable.

risks.title: Early Ioniq 5 park-pawl and driveshaft campaigns
risks.detail: REC-005448 applies to selected 2021–2022 cars’ Shift Control Unit software (roll-away risk). REC-005940 covers defective driveshafts in selected 2023 cars. Check the exact VIN; these free remedies are separate from the later ICCU action.
risks.priceBasis: A$0 for the official VIN-applicable recall remedy. This is rectification of an identified campaign, not a future owner-paid replacement quote.
risks.warranty: Check the VIN and campaign completion with the Australian manufacturer; official recall rectification is separate from ordinary warranty expiry.

items.finding: Four exact configuration snapshots re-read: original AWD A$44,990 EGC (corrected from drive-away); MY23 Dynamiq A$41,900 EGC; MY23 Techniq A$46,950 EGC; new 84-kWh QLD median A$70,490 DA (A$69,990–70,990, n=2). Australian brochures confirm 72.6 / 77.4 / 84 kWh grouping and 430 / 507 / 454 / 570 km WLTP by configuration. AC maximum is 10.5 kW; 350 kW denotes infrastructure, not a verified car peak. Preserve the MY26 PDF’s WLTP/ADR consumption-footnote conflict. MY23 Dynamiq/Techniq lack Epiq’s heat pump and conditioning; MY26 includes both.

Original AWD has a named three-restraint trial; MY23 is related evidence, not a new installation. Room and access observations are stronger than anchor count alone. No three-booster buckling evidence; ANCAP separately records one selected booster failing centre fit. Facelift arrangement stays unverified. Brochures confirm rear vents and 527-L old / 520-L refreshed VDA rear boots.

Original private-use cover is five years with unlimited km, not retrospective seven. Vehicles first registered from 1 June 2025 can get two extra years through required dealer servicing; remaining cover transfers. HV battery is 8 years / 160,000 km; current terms cover SOH below 70% with conditions and permit repair/reconditioned remedies. Original used-car terms still govern. 12V cover is 2 years / 40,000 km.

MY22 passport: 12 months / 15,000 km; MY23 normal: 24 months / 30,000 km. MY23 manual p9-8 separately requires low-conductivity coolant at 36 months / 60,000 km, 12V inspection at 12 months / 15,000 km and brake fluid every 24 months; standard coolant initially at 10 years / 200,000 km. No current all-inclusive Australian coolant tariff found. Add facelift allowance A$403/year from reported first ten-year scheduled total A$4,025. Early/MY23 allowances retain low confidence.

Re-read insurer’s model premium: Youi mean A$1,851, rounded dashboard A$1,850 unchanged. Published band A$1,142–2,234 uses its stated 80%-within-or-below criterion; November 2025–May 2026 policies. National mixed trims; no Queensland household quote or exact-variant sample. Dashboard broader bounds remain illustrative.

Budget aftermarket audit, 18 October 2026. 255/45R20 105Y XL replacement reference: A$1,156 for four fitted; 235/55R19 105W replacement reference: A$900 for four fitted. Common 40,000 km life is an illustrative assumption, not model-specific wear evidence. Prices and annual savings are estimates; check the real placard and local fitted quote.

Official ICCU recall REC-006224 supersedes REC-005942 with free software; separate selected-VIN park-pawl/driveshaft remedies are also free. Reported 15-year / 300,000-km ICCU extension still needs written Australian VIN terms; Drive re-fetch blocked, so not promoted to a verified contract. No defensible Australian annual failure/bill distribution found: retain reserves A$1,200 / 1,000 / 1,100 / 700 as low-confidence savings, not fault predictions.

ProductReview remains 3.8/5, n=8, mixed owners and two identified expert borrowed-car posts. CarsGuide exact MY23 Dynamiq 7.5/10 and EV Central base 84-kWh 4/5 retained. Add Carsales exact MY23 Techniq 85/100 (8.5/10). ReDriven’s 2026 used verdict is qualitative; its unscoped pooled 2% fault claim does not become an annual probability.

Brochures specify 1,600-kg braked towing with 100-kg towball and vehicle limits; ANCAP 2021 applies except N, expires December 2027. QLD private electric registration + traffic fee + Class 1 CTP is A$782.15–798.15 as at 1 October 2026. Used price drops do not establish future depreciation. Inspect underbody, warranty/service/recall records and charging; budget remaining warranty by first registration.
